Tucker3 tensor model across strata

Source: R/model-tucker3.R
tucker3.Rd

Joint model of the array of log rates [age, period, stratum] (or of centred log-ratio transformed life-table deaths, transform = "coda") through a Tucker3 decomposition X = G x1 A x2 B x3 C with ranks ranks = c(age, period, stratum), estimated by higher-order orthogonal iteration (HOOI; De Lathauwer, De Moor and Vandewalle 2000). The period factors (columns of B) are forecast as a multivariate random walk with drift (bootstrap of joint year-to-year changes, which keeps their correlation) or with ARIMA/ETS models per column (ts = "arima", "ets", package forecast).

Usage

tucker3(
  ranks = c(3, 3, 2),
  transform = c("log", "coda"),
  ts = c("rwd", "arima", "ets"),
  residual_noise = TRUE,
  maxit = 200,
  tol = 1e-08
)

Arguments

ranks

Tucker ranks for age, period and stratum, or "bic" / "aic" to choose them by an information criterion on the training data (n log(RSS / n) plus the penalty times the number of parameters of the factor matrices and the core; ranks up to 6 for age and period and up to 4 for strata). For selection by forecast accuracy use tuned().

transform

"log" or "coda".

ts

Forecast method for the period factors: "rwd", "arima", "ets".

residual_noise

Add the in-sample residual variation (per age and stratum, normal on the transformed scale) to the draws. It represents structure that the low-rank model does not capture. The residuals also contain the observation noise of the training years, so predictive draws, which add observation noise, are wider than the residual variation alone implies. On simulated data with period trends that the ranks do not capture, this widening brought predictive intervals close to their nominal coverage; for data that the low-rank model describes well, the intervals are too wide, and residual_noise = FALSE fits better.

maxit, tol

Settings of the HOOI iterations.

Value

A model specification.

Details

The model is experimental: tensor decompositions have been proposed for mortality of several populations, but this specification has no published evaluation; compare it with established models such as li_lee() in a backtest before using it.

With transform = "coda", life-table deaths (from age x0, the first grid age) form a composition over the age cells including the open interval; the open interval's death rate is forecast as an auxiliary random walk with drift on its log, so the open age group is kept.

Ranks are reduced to the array dimensions where needed, so the model also runs with one stratum or one age group.

References

De Lathauwer L, De Moor B, Vandewalle J (2000). On the best rank-1 and rank-(R1, R2, ..., RN) approximation of higher-order tensors. SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 21(4): 1324-1342. doi:10.1137/S0895479898346995

Kolda TG, Bader BW (2009). Tensor decompositions and applications. SIAM Review 51(3): 455-500. doi:10.1137/07070111X

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fit <- mt_fit(tucker3(ranks = c(3, 3, 2)), x)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
